title: Product of threshold signs
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X,Y:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ each have the standard Gaussian distribution under $\mu$. Define $\sigma(r)=1$ for $r\ge0$ and $\sigma(r)=-1$ for $r<0$. Then $\int \sigma(X)\sigma(Y)\,d\mu=4\mu(X\le0,\,Y\le0)-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ has the standard Gaussian distribution under $\mu$
$Y$ has the standard Gaussian distribution under $\mu$
